reading: Each single coloured cell's Chebyshev distance from the grid centre picks a ring; the output is concentric square rings around the centre, each ring painted the colour of the single cell at that distance.

slots.centre: the grid's centre cell (grids are odd-sized squares)
slots.sources: the isolated non-background cells, one per Chebyshev distance 0..r
slots.ring_colour(d): colour of the source cell whose Chebyshev distance from the centre is d
slots.output: every cell gets ring_colour(Chebyshev distance to centre)

why: on every pair the sources occupy distinct distances 0..(n-1)/2 and every output cell equals the colour of the source at its own distance

reading: Objects fall to the grid edge by shape: hollow rectangles (rings) slide straight up to the top, plus/cross shapes slide straight down to the bottom, stacking on whatever they meet in their columns.

slots.direction: up for closed hollow rectangles, down for plus/cross shapes
slots.stop: grid border or the first object already settled in its columns (stacking)

why: every object keeps its shape and columns; rings end touching the top or a ring above them, crosses end touching the bottom or a cross below them

reading: Every coloured cell with no orthogonally adjacent coloured cell (a lone cell under 4-connectivity) turns from 2 to 1.

new_rows.name: lone4
new_rows.datalog:
has4(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0, off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, px(Y2, X, D), D > 0.
has4(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0, off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, px(Y, X2, D), D > 0.
lone4(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0, !has4(Y, X).

why: exactly the colour-2 cells with no 2 among their 4 orthogonal neighbours become 1; diagonal contact does not count (so 'markers' is too strict); colour 0 is used explicitly because in one pair 2 is the most common colour

reading: The grid holds several same-size squares with an 8 border and a 2-pattern inside, among 8 noise; all squares share one inner pattern except one, and the output is that odd square cut out.

slots.candidates: the 8-bordered squares (border colour 8, interior of 2s and 8s), all of equal size
slots.odd: the square whose interior 2/8 pattern differs from all the others
slots.output: the odd square's box including its 8 border

why: on every pair exactly one square's interior pattern is unique and the output equals that square cut from the input
invariants: the cut square's cells are copied unchanged

reading: Four same-coloured cells that form the corners of a rectangle get the cells strictly inside that rectangle filled with 2.

new_rows.name: inrect
new_rows.datalog: inrect(Y, X) :- cell(Y1, X1, C), cell(Y1, X2, C), cell(Y2, X1, C), cell(Y2, X2, C), Y1 < Y2, X1 < X2, px(Y, X, D), Y > Y1, Y < Y2, X > X1, X < X2.

why: every cell strictly inside a rectangle whose four corners are coloured cells becomes 2; nothing else changes

reading: One panel holds a small line pattern (vertical and horizontal coloured lines with fixed crossing priority), separated by 5s from a panel whose edges carry 4-markers; the output is the marker panel's size with the pattern's lines redrawn on the rows and columns the 4s mark.

slots.template: the panel left (or right) of the 5 separator: background with full vertical lines and full horizontal lines, each one colour; crossing cells show which line is on top
slots.marker_panel: the other panel, background plus 4 cells on its edges
slots.line_positions: columns marked by 4s on the top/bottom edges get the vertical lines, rows marked by 4s on the left/right edges get the horizontal lines, matched to template lines in order
slots.output: marker panel size; lines drawn full length with template colours and template crossing priority

why: on every pair the output's line count, colours and crossing colours equal the template's, and line positions equal the 4-marked rows and columns
invariants: output size equals the marker panel

reading: The input is two equal squares: an 8 mask and a coloured pattern. The output is a block grid: block (i,j) is the mask shape painted in the colour of pattern cell (i,j), or empty when that cell is background.

slots.block(i,j): mask shape recoloured to pattern[i][j], or all background if pattern[i][j] is background
slots.output: n*n by n*n grid of blocks, n = half side

why: every output block is either empty or the mask shape in exactly the colour of the corresponding pattern cell

reading: An 8 legend panel shows small 3x3 shapes, each in its own colour. Each 5x5 box is swapped by the legend: a 2-box with a 1-pattern becomes a solid box in the colour whose legend shape matches the pattern (up to rotation/reflection); a solid coloured box becomes a 2-box with that colour's legend shape drawn in 1.

slots.legend: 8 panel holding 3x3 shapes, one per colour
slots.boxes: 5x5 boxes: either a 2 border with a 1-pattern in the 3x3 interior, or solid one colour
slots.pattern_box: replaced by a solid 5x5 of the legend colour whose shape matches its interior pattern (rotation/reflection allowed)
slots.solid_box(c): replaced by a 2-bordered box whose interior shows legend shape c in 1 (as drawn in the legend)

why: on every pair each box's output is determined by the legend lookup of its pattern or its colour

reading: Every pair of orthogonally adjacent 2-cells (a domino) gets a 3 outline drawn in all background cells around it; single 2-cells are left alone.

new_rows.name: domino_halo
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dom(O) :- osize(O, N), N = 2, obj(O, Y, X), obj(O, Y, X2), X2 = X + 1.
dom(O) :- osize(O, N), N = 2, obj(O, Y, X), obj(O, Y2, X), Y2 = Y + 1.
domino_halo(Y2, X2) :- dom(O), obj(O, Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C), !cell(Y2, X2, C).

why: exactly the background cells 8-adjacent to a two-cell straight object become 3; lone cells get nothing

reading: A key row of k colours sits above a slanted staircase band of 5s; the band is recoloured in steps of k rows along its diagonal, each step painted as nested L-shaped layers from the step's leading corner using key[0..k-1], the last key colour filling the rest.

slots.key: the short multi-colour row (left to right) at the top
slots.steps: band cut every k rows, each step's corner shifted k columns along the slant
slots.colour(cell): key[min(dy, dx, k-1)] where dy, dx are the cell's offsets from its step's corner (row offset, column offset toward the band interior)

why: every 5 cell is replaced by a key colour following the repeating nested-L layer pattern; no other cell changes
